gaps: Pages the design doesn't cover still show placeholder or empty content to anonymous visitors. /learning-strategies (src/app/(learning)/learning-strategies/page.tsx) is all '[Placeholder: …]' text. /resources says 'Links and categorized resources will be listed here soon.' Both are in src/app/sitemap.ts PUBLIC_PAGES. The design hides /projects and /history for exactly this reason but leaves these two published and indexed.

The privacy policy and terms (src/app/(public)/privacy-policy/page.tsx, terms-of-service/page.tsx) are not in any work package. They promise things the design removes: 'Account basics (name, email) supplied during … single-sign-on', 'Session cookies keep you signed in', 'export or request deletion … via Settings', server-side telemetry retention and account purging. They also say nothing about the new reality: notebook text, lab code and progress are kept in this browser's localStorage, with export, import and reset on /settings.

FEATURE_FLAGS_FORCE_ON is not a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable and next.config.mjs has no `env` entry, so the client bundle never sees it. ACCOUNTS_ENABLED and SITE_FEATURES (aiTutor, simulation) would then be true during the server render and false after hydration. ClientProviders would render SessionProvider on the server but not on the client, useAuth would pick different branches, and Feynman/Notebook AI controls would differ, giving hydration mismatches. The architecture's 'or turned on by FEATURE_FLAGS_FORCE_ON' is wrong for client code. Fix: derive client-visible switches only from NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables, or expose FORCE_ON through next.config `env`. Also make E2E_ACCOUNTS set NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_FLAG_AI_TUTOR and NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_FLAG_SIMULATION, not just FORCE_ON.

With accounts on, signed-out visitors are blocked again, which contradicts 'signed-out learners keep the local store'. The gates are build-time only:
- SITE_FEATURES.aiTutor shows the AI widget, Teach-it-back AI feedback and Notebook AI to signed-out visitors, who then get 401 'Sign in to use the AI tutor.'
- simulationAvailable={SITE_FEATURES.simulation} is baked into the static lab page, so 'Run workspace' sends POST /api/simulate and gets 401.
- Navbar's NotificationCenter fetches /api/me/notifications whenever accountUI is on, so signed-out visitors see 'Unable to load notifications'.
Each of these controls needs to also check usePersistenceTarget().target==='server' and fall back to the local or 'Run it on your simulator' UI.

The re-enable plan has no sign-in entry point. UserMenu only shows 'Not signed in' and Settings, plus Sign out when a user is signed in, and the lab redirect is being removed. Once accounts return, the only way to sign in is typing /api/auth/signin. Step 6 should add a Sign in action and a sign-in prompt for the first-sign-in import.

Re-enable ordering can look like data loss. Step 2 switches signed-in learners' labs (and placement) to the server stores, but /api/me/import comes only at step 5. On first sign-in, all local lab progress disappears from the UI. The dashboard also keeps reading local lab records while signed-in labs write to the server, so its 'labs in progress' goes stale. Either make import a prerequisite for target 'server', or have the account lab store merge with or fall back to local data.

localStorage budget and quota risks:
- sanitizeWorkspace allows up to 1 MB per lab, so 23 labs could reach about 23 MB, not the stated '≤1 MB total'.
- The notebook is one key holding up to 500 × 8000 = 4M characters. Several engines (WebKit in particular) count about 2 bytes per UTF-16 unit against roughly 5 MB, so the worst case alone can exceed the quota.
- With one shared origin quota, one oversized record makes writes of other records (activity, flashcards) fail too, and the 'memory overlay' loses them on reload.
- A 3.5 MB warning based on character count may fire only after the quota is already hit.
Suggested fixes: store notebook entries as keyed records, lower the caps, measure 2 bytes per character, and warn earlier.

Cross-tab and stale-snapshot overwrites can lose data:
- The lab record is one object holding fileBuffers, completedSteps and stepEvidence. A stale second tab that autosaves its in-memory record would erase a completion made in another tab. saveWorkspace must be update(fn) on a fresh read that touches only fileBuffers and currentStepId, and that needs a test.
- Same-tab writes fire no 'storage' event, so legacy consumers outside the event bus never see importLearnerData or resetLearnerData. learning-route-state keeps memoryChoice and only fires ROUTE_CHANGE_EVENT from writeSelectedRoute. useExerciseProgress holds React state and its next recordAttempt writes the pre-reset attempts back.
Dispatch the legacy change events and reload after import or reset, or move those hooks onto the store.

Performance: if getSnapshot re-reads the raw localStorage string on every render to check its per-raw-string cache, then an autosaving notebook editor (up to a 4 MB key) or the flashcard record (about 200 KB) on lessons does a synchronous getItem of the whole value on every render. Use an in-memory version counter, invalidated by the event bus and 'storage' events, instead.

Flashcard edge cases the store shape doesn't handle:
- src/lib/flashcard-decks.ts has deckAliases (I-UVM-1A_Components → I-UVM-1_UVM_Intro, I-UVM-1B → I-UVM-4, I-UVM-1C → I-UVM-5). The same cards then appear under two deckIds, but cards{[cardId]} keeps a single deckId. The per-deck dynamic-import loader for /dashboard/review must resolve aliases, and due counts must not double-count.
- Three deckIds are each used by two lessons (F2C_Procedural_Constructs, I-SV-2A, I-SV-3A), so decks{deckId}.lessonHref can't hold both 'back to lesson' targets.
- scripts/check-mdx.mjs parses flashcard-decks.ts with a regex (`export const flashcardDecks … = {` and `deckAliases`), so restructuring the registry into per-deck loaders breaks it unless it is updated too.

Tests that will fail and are owned by neither WP0 nor WP1:
- tests/security-config.test.ts imports the nextauth route and expects it to throw without a secret. The route WP0 owns now imports auth lazily, so the import no longer throws; one case already fails today.
- tests/app/feature-gating.spec.tsx mocks '@/tools/featureFlags' with only isFeatureEnabled, so site-features.ts and accounts.ts, which read `featureFlags.*`, get undefined. It also asserts the old dashboard, settings, notifications and projects behaviour.
- tests/e2e/feature-flags.spec.ts now runs in the default anonymous mode and expects /dashboard to 404 and placeholder copy on /notifications and /projects.
- tests/e2e/navigation-entry-points.spec.ts:122 expects /Sign in required/.
- tests/e2e/ai-assistant-animation.spec.ts clicks 'Open AI assistant' with no flag skip.
- tests/e2e/account-preferences.spec.ts never signs in, so the server-only AccountPreferencesPanel won't render in accounts mode.
- Unit tests pinned to the removed copy or gates: LabLink.test.tsx (asserts requireSession() in page.tsx), LessonMdxPipeline.test.tsx ('Sign in to run labs.'), PracticeHub.test.tsx ('Sign in to open.'), learning-paths.test.ts ('sign-in required'), curriculum-overview.test.ts, Navbar.test.tsx, KeyboardShortcuts.test.tsx, search/shortcuts.test.ts, AIAssistantWidget.test.tsx, dashboard-page.spec.tsx (mocks curriculum-status, which is being deleted), settings-page-client.spec.tsx, PlacementQuiz.test.tsx, placement-links.spec.ts, srs.spec.ts (createFlashcard), TopicPage.test.tsx, and both useCurriculumProgress specs.

Source files the design changes that must belong to exactly one of WP2–WP7, which I couldn't see:
- Navbar.tsx (Dashboard link, notification gating) and Sidebar.tsx OUTLINE_QUICK_LINKS (the design says the outline will link Dashboard).
- search/shortcuts.ts, ShortcutsHelpDialog.tsx and layout/KeyboardShortcuts.tsx: it passes the whole featureFlags object to shortcutRoute, so it must change together with ShortcutFlags.
- (learning)/layout.tsx (AI widget gate) and lab-registry.ts (labRequiresSignIn, which WP1 doesn't list).
- sitemap.ts plus tests/app/sitemap.test.ts (adding labs).

CI coverage for the account seam disappears. .github/workflows/quality-gates.yml runs `test:e2e:release` straight through playwright.config.ts and never sets E2E_ACCOUNTS. After the change, nothing in CI exercises the code that has to work when accounts return: createAccountLabProgressStore, AccountPreferencesPanel, the placement server POST, SessionProvider/useSessionAuth and the nextauth delegate path. Add an E2E_ACCOUNTS job, or at least unit tests for those paths with a mocked session. CI also exports AUTH_TEST_MODE=true and DATABASE_URL globally, so the 'anonymous default' must override them explicitly rather than with `??`.

Community is inconsistent with the design's own rule that features needing several users' data are hidden until accounts exist. SITE_FEATURES.community is featureFlags.community alone, while aiTutor and simulation also require ACCOUNTS_ENABLED. If an operator turns community on without accounts, CommunityPageClient shows 'Sign in to join the conversation' while /api/auth/* answers 404. Make it featureFlags.community && ACCOUNTS_ENABLED.

Guarding the server-only modules: src/server/persistence-gate.ts has no `server-only` guard. If a 'use client' module ever imports it, webpack still resolves the lazy import('@/lib/auth') into the client graph, pulling in node:crypto and the Prisma proxy. Add an ESLint no-restricted-imports rule for src/server/** in client files, or install `server-only`.

Imported backups are untrusted input. importLearnerData accepts any user-chosen JSON file, and the notebook gets edit and 'Download as Markdown'. The design should say that notebook bodies and titles are always rendered as plain text, never MDX or HTML. It should also say how legacy keys are validated on import: only read-only readers are defined for them, with no parse, but the bundle includes them.

verdict:
Feasible, but fix the items below before the work packages are split. I checked the main assumptions against the code and they hold:
- **Graders:** src/lib/lab-graders.ts imports nothing and never touches Buffer or process. Only 2 of the 23 available labs use a grader (sv-basics-v2, sv-selfcheck-v1), and neither needs a sandbox.
- **Lab page:** it can become static the same way lessons are. lesson-loader already reads files with fs at build time and is served prerendered. Nothing on the lab page calls headers(), cookies() or useSearchParams.
- **Pages that read the database:** /settings, /history and /notifications are the only ones that call requireSession or Prisma. /dashboard, /dashboard/notebook and /dashboard/memory-hub are flag-only shells.
- **SessionProvider:** it is the only caller of /api/auth/session. Nothing calls useSession except AuthContext, so turning it off when accounts are off is safe.
- **Flashcard ids:** 1675 cards, 30 without ids (A-UVM-1, -2, -3), no duplicate ids, and no deck registered under two ids.
- **Test baseline:** the 18 affected vitest files pass today (132 tests).

The problems that block the plan:
- **The flags don't match between server and client.** FEATURE_FLAGS_FORCE_ON only reaches the server, so the browser ignores it.
- **The package order breaks the live site and the tests.** WP0 makes /api/auth return 404 while the lab page still redirects there. WP1 breaks a test owned by another package. The deploy happens on every push.
- **Several existing tests will crash or fail and aren't listed.**
- **Some data in the browser store can be lost:** legacy keys stored as bare strings, a single large notebook record, autosave writing over corrupt records, edits from two tabs, and Safari deleting storage after 7 days.

The design text I was given stops partway through WP1. I could not check file ownership for WP2–WP7 directly. The ownership problems below are inferred from the code.
gaps: The flags differ between server and browser. src/lib/persistence/accounts.ts sets ACCOUNTS_ENABLED from featureFlags.accountUI. featureFlags.ts reads process.env.FEATURE_FLAGS_FORCE_ON, which has no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix, and next.config.mjs has no env block. So the browser always sees it as undefined, while the server reads it at build time for prerendered pages and at runtime for dynamic routes. The design's claim that FEATURE_FLAGS_FORCE_ON turns accounts on is only true on the server. The same applies to aiTutor and simulation in SITE_FEATURES. Example: in E2E_ACCOUNTS mode, if only FORCE_ON is set, the server renders the AI widget, the simulation panel and the account seams but the browser doesn't, which causes hydration mismatches. /api/feature-flags (force-static) also reports server values. Fix: don't let FORCE_ON apply to accountUI, aiTutor or simulation, or expose it through next.config env. Also add NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_FLAG_AI_TUTOR and NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_FLAG_SIMULATION to featureFlagEnv in run-e2e-tests.cjs and to the env in playwright.config.ts.

Package order breaks the live site between WP0 and WP1. WP0 makes /api/auth/* return 404. Until WP1 lands, practice/lab/[labId]/page.tsx still sends a 307 to /api/auth/signin, so every lab link ends in a 404 on the Worker, because each push to curriculum-quality-program deploys. tests/e2e/regression-gates.spec.ts 'LabLink validation' (expects status < 400) and authenticateTestLearner (/api/auth/csrf now 404 in the new anonymous default) both fail. Land WP0's auth-route change and e2e default together with WP1, or keep the nextauth route as it is until WP1.

WP1 breaks a test it doesn't own. tests/components/LabLink.test.tsx (lines 101–112) reads page.tsx and asserts it contains 'requireSession()' and the notFound regex, and it imports labRequiresSignIn from src/lib/lab-registry.ts. Neither file is in WP1's list. As soon as WP1 removes requireSession, its acceptance check ('full vitest has no new failures') can't pass. WP1 needs to own LabLink.test.tsx and lab-registry.ts (toLearnerLabDto, labRequiresSignIn), or depend on the lab-entry package.

Existing vitest mocks will crash once pages import the new modules. tests/app/feature-gating.spec.tsx and tests/placement-links.spec.ts mock '@/tools/featureFlags' with only isFeatureEnabled. Vitest throws on access to an export the mock doesn't define, so any page that now imports site-features.ts or persistence/accounts.ts (which read featureFlags.* when they load) fails at import. That includes the placement page via PlacementQuiz → usePersistenceTarget, the settings shell, the dashboard and notifications. Either have accounts.ts and site-features.ts call isFeatureEnabled(), or update those mocks to use importOriginal.

These tests will break and are not listed in WP0 or WP1, so each needs an owner:
- feature-gating.spec.tsx (dashboard and settings notFound, notifications and projects placeholder copy)
- placement-links.spec.ts (dashboard hidden, assessment link shown)
- PlacementQuiz.test.tsx (expects fetch POST /api/me/assessments at line 77, and 'Go to dashboard' only with tracking)
- PracticeHub.test.tsx ('Sign in to open.')
- LessonMdxPipeline.test.tsx ('Sign in to run labs.')
- learning-paths.test.ts ('sign-in required')
- curriculum-overview.test.ts
- search/shortcuts.test.ts ({tracking, community} flags)
- KeyboardShortcuts.test.tsx
- Navbar.test.tsx
- dashboard-page.spec.tsx (mocks curriculum-status, which is being deleted)
- settings-page-client.spec.tsx
- srs.spec.ts (the createFlashcard case; keep the review and due cases)
- TopicPage.test.tsx
- sitemap.test.ts (PUBLIC_PAGES vs the lab URLs)
- hooks/useCurriculumProgress.test.ts and unit/useCurriculumProgress.spec.ts (isLoaded semantics under the external store)
- flashcard-registry.test.ts, expert-flashcards.spec.ts, amba-flashcards.spec.ts (they import the default flashcardDecks map)

These e2e specs fail in the new anonymous default mode and need an owner or the requireAccountsMode guard:
- ai-assistant-animation.spec.ts (the widget is hidden)
- navigation-entry-points.spec.ts ('Sign in required' description)
- feature-flags.spec.ts (runs when no flags are set. It expects /dashboard to 404, which is now false, and notifications and projects placeholder copy, which are now 404s)
- account-preferences.spec.ts and navigation.spec.ts (accountUI cases)

A build script is missing from the plan. scripts/check-mdx.mjs (line 64) parses src/lib/flashcard-decks.ts with the regex /export const flashcardDecks[^=]*=\s*\{([\s\S]*?)\n\};/. Splitting the deck registry for per-deck dynamic import must keep that exact export shape, or check-mdx breaks too.

Probable file collisions in the packages I couldn't see:
- src/components/curriculum/LessonPractice.tsx contains the lab copy 'Sign in to run labs.', the FlashcardWidget whose deck should be resolved on the server, and FeynmanPromptWidget (Teach-it-back). That is three features in one file.
- tests/app/feature-gating.spec.tsx and tests/e2e/feature-flags.spec.ts each cover dashboard, settings, notifications, projects and community, which belong to different packages.
- src/app/(learning)/layout.tsx mounts AIAssistantWidget directly, so the aiTutor gate needs an owner.
- Navbar.tsx and KeyboardShortcuts.tsx both import featureFlags directly: shortcutRoute(id, featureFlags) won't type-check once ShortcutFlags becomes {dashboard, community}.

The shared lab policy doesn't fit the data the client gets. checkGradedSubmission(lab, …) and sanitizeWorkspace(lab, …) need lab.assets (the editable paths), but LearnerLabDto (src/types/lab.ts) leaves out assets, and toLearnerLabDto lives in lab-registry.ts, which WP1 doesn't own. Give the policy a narrower input, for example {steps, graderId, editablePaths}, built from files[]. Also, the route's size check uses Buffer.byteLength. The shared module must use TextEncoder, or the browser build breaks.

Lesson pages could grow by about 98 KB. LabProgressBadge (on lesson, Practice Hub and home cards) needs each lab's step count and version. If it imports src/generated/lab-registry.ts (98 KB) or lab-registry.ts in client code, every lesson page grows and may exceed the app/curriculum/[...slug]/page gzip budget in docs/bundle-baseline.json. Pass {labId, version, stepCount} as props instead.

Backup can't handle the legacy keys as specified. ROUTE_STORAGE_KEY ('svuvm.learningRoute') is stored as a bare string such as 'junior', not JSON, so a backup bundle defined as 'entries{[key]: parsed JSON}' fails on JSON.parse or drops it. legacy.ts is read-only, so importing the exercise and route keys has no defined writer or validator. useExerciseProgress (useState) and learning-route-state (its own event, 'svuvm:learning-route-change') don't listen to the new store's event bus. After an import or reset they keep stale state and can write it back. Fix: store raw strings for legacy keys and reload the page after import or reset.

Data-loss risks:
- Autosave can erase recoverable data. 'Corrupt reads as empty and is not overwritten until an explicit write' doesn't help for records written automatically: lab autosave (today it fires 600 ms after mount even without an edit), curriculumProgress on every visit, the activity log and the lesson log. A corrupt record would be replaced within one page view. Copy the corrupt raw value to a side key first, and autosave labs only after a user edit.
- Notebook as one record. The notebook is one record of up to about 4 MB that is rewritten on every autosave. Hitting the quota makes every note memory-only at once. Use defineKeyedRecord, one key per entry.
- Two open tabs on the same lab can ping-pong saves or overwrite each other's edits. Sync only steps and status across tabs, not editor buffers, or skip writes when the value is identical.
- Safari deletes script-written storage for sites the person hasn't used in 7 days. Add backup reminders.
- Old lab-version keys are never pruned, so they keep filling the quota.

Due counts can include cards that no longer exist. countDueCards(data, now) counts only local SRS state, so cards whose ids were removed or renamed in content keep counting toward 'N due' on the dashboard and lessons, and the review queue can't render them. Check local states against the current card ids of each deck.

The Worker and SSR guarantees aren't enforced:
- dynamic='error' is optional. Make it required on the lab page, and add a check that .next/prerender-manifest.json lists all 23 /practice/lab/<id> routes. A cf:preview smoke test of a lab page and of an unknown id (404) is not in any acceptance list.
- safeStorage's 'no window → memory Map' would share data across requests inside the Worker if anything ever writes during SSR. Server-side writes should do nothing, and the window 'storage' listener must be guarded.
- /notifications keeps force-dynamic, because the dynamic export can't be conditional. Its notFound() when accounts are off still costs a dynamic Worker render (100–500 ms of CPU) on every hit.

A half-configured accounts deploy keeps making failed requests. Example: accountUI is set but the Google keys are missing. The browser mounts SessionProvider while the server gate returns 404 for /api/auth/session and /_log on every page mount and tab focus. Return 200 {} for /session when the server isn't configured, or base the browser-side mount on a build-time NEXT_PUBLIC indicator that the server is configured.

Minor:
- isServerPersistenceConfigured(env) can't vary ACCOUNTS_ENABLED through its env parameter (it's fixed when the module loads), so the planned 'environment combinations' test needs a module mock.
- Next already aliases 'server-only' (next/dist/compiled/server-only), so the guard could be used with a vitest alias instead of being dropped.
- With all flags forced on, accounts-mode e2e shows CodeExecutionEnvironment with no queue env configured, so its 'Run workspace' button returns SIMULATION_EXECUTION_NOT_CONFIGURED.
